title: Bad Trips Guide, Round 59
intro: Round 59 (2026-11-25). Your charcoal and poison control paragraphs are in, word for word, and the two read [Human High in one window](https://www.pangram.com/history/7b62fe4a-c50a-4bbc-9c3b-1fcf7448e3a6). The link to the remedy entry is back on "Activated charcoal", and the review's link is on "The usual advice", since the hour is what that review says. What I got wrong is [here](https://github.com/u-dont-existDOTcom/joel-articles/blob/main/docs/lessons/2026-11-25-1743-bad-trips.md): I kept a model's advice from your post (ask poison control about charcoal) as if it were yours, and I wrote a rule measured on pure, fast drugs into a guide about plant medicines. [Each point of your answer and where it went](https://github.com/u-dont-existDOTcom/joel-articles/blob/main/articles/bad-trips/review/r58/RESULTS-R58.md).

Two more paragraphs now read Human High by themselves, both in My Acute Rescue Remedies and both in the guide ([every check](https://github.com/u-dont-existDOTcom/joel-articles/blob/main/articles/bad-trips/humanize/h77-20261125/RESULTS.md)). In "Nausea, heat, exhaustion ..." four words changed ("all get read as spiritual signs" for "all become spiritual content"): Low, then Medium, then [High](https://www.pangram.com/history/6058dbfc-dc05-444e-b564-51b72e8acc74). The gut-driven paragraph is card 2.
After these the work goes down [the list of what is left](https://github.com/u-dont-existDOTcom/joel-articles/blob/main/articles/bad-trips/humanize/h77-20261125/LEFT.md), starting with the gut tools.

suggestions.title: 1. Swallowed Too Much?: one clause of your poison control paragraph
suggestions.whose: his own: the paragraph from his round-58 answer; the two sentences I suggest are mine
suggestions.question:
Your paragraph is in as you wrote it. One clause I'd say differently: "even if they often can't give actionable advice for liability reasons". What you told me is one case, about charcoal ("poison control said they aren't allowed to tell them to take charcoal"), and your next sentence says they do help with first aid instructions. [Poison Control's own page](https://www.poison.org/articles/2017-jun/activated-charcoal) says of charcoal that "it is not recommended to use these products at home to treat a poisoning", so anyone who asks them about it will hear what the person you know heard. This version says that, with the link on "they aren't allowed to tell anyone to take it", and reads [Human High, 74 words in one window](https://www.pangram.com/history/9afb6a77-e533-49d1-8f65-b20306e090ca) on its first check:
"If you're unsure about the interactions between the drugs taken, it could be helpful to check with AI & Poison Control. They might have important info, especially if the drugs are well-known. They can also help you with standard first aid instructions. But I wouldn't ask Poison Control about charcoal. Someone I know did, and came away very confused after being told they aren't allowed to tell anyone to take it."
(a) leave yours as it is; (b) this one; or your own words.
suggestions.why: your clause says more than your case shows ("often", "for liability reasons"), and the reader who does ask about charcoal is not told what will happen
suggestions.stays: your paragraph, which is in the guide now
suggestions.advice_note: (b); fairly sure. It keeps your three sentences word for word and adds only what happened to the person you know

suggestions.title: 2. My Acute Rescue Remedies: two things a reader in the moment couldn't tell
suggestions.whose: the post's paragraph, drafted by a model, with your own last line kept word for word ("A gut-driven mental hell is often mistaken as shadow work.")
suggestions.question:
This paragraph is in and reads [Human High, 75 words in one window](https://www.pangram.com/history/8f7d99cd-1a1e-4b29-b0e5-0b1e1659c02a); your post's read [AI, High](https://www.pangram.com/history/a378ba15-aee0-4b83-9ca8-702971cc31c6). Every sign is kept, and "a different branch" is now "the remedies below" and "the shadow work further down". Two things a fresh reader, sitting with a friend who has diarrhea and says their mind is going crazy, couldn't get from it, and only you know the answers:
2.1 What would a friend actually see when someone has "loss of bodily control" or "neurological disorganization"?
2.2 Diarrhea and nausea are common on a psychedelic anyway. How do you tell a gut-driven mental hell from a mainly emotional crisis while it is happening?
A line or two from you on either and I'll put it in; or (a) leave the paragraph as it is.
suggestions.why: the section holds no answer to either, and a guess from me would be a model's advice in your guide again
suggestions.stays: the paragraph as it now reads
suggestions.advice_note: your answer to 2.2, even one sentence: it is the question the whole section turns on
